results.title: Cold Open
results.description: Pure black screen. A child's voice speaks into the dark — present tense, quiet, real. The first sound of the film is a kid telling us he hasn't eaten today.
results.vo_quote: I didn't eat lunch today. My mom said I shouldn't.
results.notes: BLACK SCREEN. AUDIO ONLY. The voice should be a real Davis County kid if possible — gentle, matter-of-fact, no theatrics. Eight seconds of black before any image. This is the hook — the audience leans in immediately. Whatever else they were thinking about disappears.

results.title: Wide Establishing — The Village
results.description: Wide cinematic establishing shot of the Ogden Christmas Village at night. Beautiful watercolor world — wet cobblestones, decorated trees, lampposts with golden halos, distant warmly-lit shops, dense painterly snow. No main characters yet. We're being shown where the legend begins.
results.vo_quote: A few years ago, on a cold night in Ogden, a man walked up to the Giving Machines.
results.notes: Establishing the world. Tone: warm, slightly nostalgic, like a story being told. Color leans warm-yellow-amber (memory/past). Real Light-the-World Giving Machines visible at frame edge with their official branding.

results.title: Doug at the Machines
results.description: Doug — the volunteer — stands beside the three Giving Machines, hands in his coat pockets, waiting. The picture of a regular kind man doing a regular kind thing on a cold night. Unaware he's about to witness something he'll talk about for the rest of his life.
results.notes: Doug should feel at home here — relaxed, calm. Not a saint, not a salesman. Just a guy who signed up to volunteer.

results.title: The Approach
results.description: A man walks slowly toward the machines through the falling snow. Worn coat. Beanie. He doesn't look like the typical Giving Machines donor — and that's the whole point. We don't know yet what he's about to do.
results.vo_quote: He didn't look like he had much. But he had walked a long way to get there.
results.notes: The man's gait should be deliberate, not hesitant. He came here on purpose. Background other figures are dark silhouettes walking in the village.

results.title: Two-Shot at the Machine
results.description: Doug shows the man the donation options — including the school lunch one. The machines glow between them. This is the moment a stranger learns what ten dollars can do.
results.vo_quote: This one feeds a kid for a week. Ten dollars buys a child their school lunch.
results.notes: Doug's gesture should be matter-of-fact, not pitching. He's just explaining the options the way he would to anyone. The man is listening intently — he's the one feeling the weight, not Doug.

results.title: The Recognition
results.description: Extreme close-up on the man's face. Something has just landed inside him. Nothing dramatic — just a small change behind the eyes. We don't know yet what he's remembering. We only know he's somewhere else for a moment.
results.vo_quote: Somebody did that for me once.
results.notes: THE EMOTIONAL HERO SHOT. The line lands gently — almost to himself. The catchlight in the eye does the heavy lifting. No tears, no theatrics. Just a man who suddenly remembers being eight years old at a cafeteria table.  // 2026-05-19: hard cut to flashback (#7) lands on this line.

results.title: The Boy — Flashback (1980s)
results.description: FLASHBACK — what the man is remembering, shown not told. Hard cut from the man's face (#6). Same composition as Mateo's table (Movement II) — a boy alone at the end of a cafeteria table — but a lunch tray slides IN from off-frame. The boy looks up. Hold one beat on his hazel eyes — the SAME eyes as the man at the machines — then cut back. This is the seed of the loop.
results.notes: KEYSTONE (decision locked 2026-05-19). ~3–4 sec, lives inside the Recognition beat so runtime barely moves. Warm-yellow MEMORY tone to match Movement I. The tray ARRIVES here (the boy gets fed) — it rhymes against Mateo's EMPTY space, where no tray has come yet. Eyes must match the man (#6) and pay off at the loop (#23).

results.title: He Walks Away
results.description: The man turns and walks away into the village. Doug is left behind. We don't know yet if the story is over or just starting.
results.notes: The audience should feel a small pull of disappointment here — did he just leave? That's intentional. The pause lets the return mean more.

results.title: Boots in the Snow
results.description: Tight on a pair of worn boots crunching through fresh snow. He came back. We don't know what he came back with.
results.notes: No characters above the boots. Just the boots, the snow, the soft golden glow of the wet pavement. Quiet, intimate, anticipatory.

results.title: The Bill
results.description: The man's hand extending a folded $20 bill. Worn, creased, real. The only thing in sharp focus.
results.vo_quote: I want to buy the lunches. Will you take cash?
results.notes: The bill matters. It's not new. It's been folded and unfolded. It came from a pocket, not a wallet.

results.title: Doug's Reaction
results.description: Doug's face as he understands what's happening. The bill he's been handed is not the donation. It's everything this man has.
results.vo_quote: I'm sorry — I don't have change for a twenty.
results.notes: Doug should not look pitying — that would patronize the man. He's matter-of-fact, gentle, slightly apologetic about the practical problem.

results.title: The Pause
results.description: A beat. Two men looking at each other. The man considering. Doug waiting. The audience leaning forward.
results.notes: This shot is quiet on purpose. Let the silence sit. The next shot is the line — give it room to land.

results.title: Let's Get Two
results.description: The man with the smallest, gentlest smile. Saying the line that the entire film is named for. Calm, certain, dignified.
results.vo_quote: Let's get two, then. Somebody did this for me.
results.notes: THE LINE LANDS HERE. Don't push the emotion — let the line do the work. The man should look like he's at peace with what he's saying.

results.title: Walking Into the Light
results.description: The man walks away into the village. Smaller and smaller. Becomes part of the lights. We will not see him again. The story he started is about to belong to someone else.
results.vo_quote: He walked back into the night, and we never learned his name.
results.notes: This is the handoff — the man's story ends here. Everything from this point forward is the story of a kid we have not yet met.

results.title: Transition — From Then to Now
results.description: The warm yellow lamplight of the village dissolves into the warm yellow morning sun of a Davis County school cafeteria. Same color, different decade. Same story, different child.
results.vo_quote: His story is the reason we tell this one.
results.notes: TYPOGRAPHY/COMP TRANSITION — built in After Effects. Cross-dissolve from the warm bokeh of the village exterior to warm bokeh of cafeteria windows. Same color palette, different setting. The film transitions from sepia-warm memory to brighter, more saturated present.  // 2026-05-19: dissolve now also rhymes the BOY's FULL tray (flashback #7) into Mateo's EMPTY space — same framing, tray vs no-tray.

results.title: Mateo at the Table
results.description: A modern Davis County school cafeteria. Bright, sunlit, warm. Other kids eating, laughing quietly. One boy sits alone at the end of a table. Backpack still on. Empty space in front of him where a tray should be. He's not unhappy — he's careful. Like he's been told what to do and he's doing it.
results.vo_quote: This is Mateo. He's eight. He's in a Davis County classroom right now.
results.notes: MATEO is the heart of the film. He needs a real face — real-proportioned eight-year-old body, cartoon face detail with expressive dot-eyes. He's not crying, not angry, not pitiful. He's QUIET. Patient. The kind of patient that doesn't belong on an eight-year-old. THE COLOR SHIFTS HERE — from warm-yellow memory to brighter, more saturated daylight present-tense. We are now in 2026, in our community.

results.title: The Empty Space
results.description: Tight on the table in front of Mateo. No tray. No food. His small hands folded. The shot we feel in our chest before we hear the line that explains it.
results.vo_quote: Mateo's family is behind. Not by much. By enough. They've decided — the way frightened people do — that it's safer for him to be hungry than seen. So he folds his hands, and waits out the lunch hour. He's good at it.
results.notes: DO NOT name immigration. Do not name a country, a status, a fear by name. The audience that needs to understand will understand. The line says enough.

results.title: The Other Kids
results.description: A wider shot of the cafeteria. Other children — also real-proportioned, also cartoon-faced — eating, talking, normal. Mateo small in the frame, alone, the only still figure.
results.vo_quote: He's not the only one. In Davis County, one in seven kids carries an unpaid lunch balance.
results.notes: Mateo is small in this frame on purpose. The audience should feel his isolation in a room full of warmth. The other kids are not background — they're cartoon-faced kids too, just not the focus.  // FACT-CHECK before final: confirm the "one in seven / unpaid lunch balance" figure for Davis County; swap in the real DEF number if different.

results.title: The Numbers
results.description: Cream watercolor background. Numbers appear in elegant red serif typography. The math of the problem.
results.vo_quote: Ten dollars buys a week. Forty, a month. Three hundred sixty dollars buys a child a year of lunches they would not otherwise eat.
results.notes: TYPOGRAPHY COMP — built in Premiere/After Effects. Cream watercolor paper background to match the film. Cormorant Garamond serif. Deep red numbers. Numbers appear one at a time, paced with the V.O.

results.title: The Tray Arrives
results.description: A lunch tray slides quietly onto the table in front of Mateo. We don't see who placed it there. He looks up — surprise, then carefully concealed relief. Nobody made a fuss. Nobody said his name. He just gets to eat.
results.vo_quote: Somebody slides a tray in front of him. He doesn't see who. He never will. That's the point.
results.notes: The hand placing the tray is OFF-FRAME — we only see the tray sliding into view. This is critical. The intervention is invisible. Mateo doesn't know who did it. His parents will never know. That's the whole point.

results.title: Mateo Eats
results.description: Mateo, mid-bite. Eyes closed slightly. The relief of a kid who hasn't eaten all day finally eating. No drama. Just lunch.
results.vo_quote: No one called his parents. No one said his name. He just got to eat.
results.notes: This is the closest thing to joy in the film. Don't oversell it. It's a kid eating lunch. That's the point — for him, that's everything.

results.title: The Wide Pull-Back
results.description: Camera pulls back. Mateo eating becomes one figure in a wide cafeteria full of other kids — some of whom are also Mateos we never met. The film opens out into the bigger picture.
results.vo_quote: There are kids in our schools right now who aren't eating. Not because food isn't there. Because shame is.
results.notes: The pullback is the whole emotional argument — Mateo is one. There are more. The audience reads it without being told.

results.title: The Loop — Three Faces
results.description: THE LOOP MADE EXPLICIT (decision locked 2026-05-19). A three-beat match-cut built in edit from existing winners: Mateo mid-bite (now) → the Boy mid-relief (1980s flashback, #7) → the Man's face at the machines (#6). Same framing, same hazel eyes, same mercy. Three kids who are the same kid. The hand that feeds is always off-frame — because the hand is the audience.
results.notes: Built in After Effects/Premiere from existing winners — depends on #7 still being generated first. Leads straight into the end card (#24).

results.title: Be the Someone
results.description: End card. Cream watercolor background. The single line the entire film has been building toward, in deep red elegant serif. Below it: the URL where viewers go to give.
results.notes: TYPOGRAPHY COMP — built in After Effects. Cream watercolor paper texture background to match the film. Cormorant Garamond serif, deep red. 'Be the someone.' large and centered, holds for 3 beats. Then 'daviskids.org/lunch-angels' appears below in slightly smaller. DEF logo bottom corner. Music swells then resolves. Black.
